memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When you beat the olives from your trees, do not go over the branches a second time. Leave what remains for the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow. When you harvest the grapes in your vineyard, do not go over the vines again. Leave what remains for the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow. - Deut 24:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God repeats and extends the principle of leaving margin for the poor. When harvesting olives, do not strip the branches a second time. When gathering grapes, do not go back over the vines. Leave what remains for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow. God did not want His people to squeeze every last bit for themselves. He wanted generosity built into the very way they worked and lived.

Notice how this generosity was not occasional or dramatic, but woven into the regular rhythms of harvest. It was a settled way of life, a habit of leaving room for others. God's people were to be characterised by a consistent, everyday openhandedness that made provision for those in need without fanfare or reluctance.

This challenges the natural human tendency to maximise for ourselves and hold on to all we can. God calls His people to a different way, one of built-in generosity, where caring for the needy is simply part of how we live and work. The New Testament calls us to be rich in good deeds, generous and willing to share (1 Tim 6:18). This kind of generosity flows from hearts that have received God's own lavish generosity in Christ, who gave everything for us. When we leave "grapes on the vine" for others, we reflect the openhanded heart of our God. How can generosity become a regular, woven-in part of your everyday life?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is generosity a regular rhythm in your life or an occasional act?
2. How does God's lavish giving in Christ shape your own?
3. What "grapes" could you leave for others this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for Your lavish generosity to me in Christ. Weave openhanded generosity into my everyday life, making room for others. Amen.
